articles.title: Andy Reid decries borderline false start that took would-be game-winning Chiefs TD off the board vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Reid described the fateful false start as "one man's opinion."
articles.body:
For a moment Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs thought they had a game-winning touchdown against the Denver Broncos.

Patrick Mahomes hit Rashee Rice for a go-ahead score as the game clock hit zero for what looked like a 30-28 Kansas City victory.

But Kansas City's celebration was short-lived.

A flag was on the field. Officials called Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore for a false start, and the touchdown was taken off the board. The Chiefs were backed up five yards, and had to run their play again, this time from the 6-yard line instead of the 1.

This time, the Broncos defense made a stop with a sack of Patrick Mahomes to end the game.

Here's a closer look at the fateful final penalty.

Moore's right hip moved slightly, and he looked to his left toward Mahomes as the play clock ticked down.

It's a movement that happens countless times each Sunday and doesn't get called. Sometimes it does, and this time it was during the highest-leverage moment of Week 8. And it cost the Chiefs a win in a 28-24 victory for the Broncos .

Chiefs coach Andy Reid wasn't convinced about the call. He described it as "one man's opinion."

"I didn't see it," Reid said in his postgame news conference. "That's one man's opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."

Regardless of Reid's opinion of the call, the result for Kansas City was relinquishment of the division lead in the AFC West. The Broncos leave Sunday's win at 6-2, a half-game ahead of the 5-2 Chiefs.

The two teams have split their season series, and the race for the division title is shaping up to be a tight one down the season's second-half stretch.

articles.title: NFL: Minnesota Vikings lose unbeaten record while Denver Broncos beat Kansas City Chiefs
articles.summary: A wild weekend in the NFL saw Joe Burrow and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers make history, while Lamar Jackson was sidelined on his return from injury.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend.

There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime.

The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again.

Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass.

And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson.

Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL.

Jackson returns - but immediately injured again

Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills.

But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury.

That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners.

The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery.

This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year.

Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.

NFL's Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury

Minnesota put their 6-0 record on the line at their NFC North rivals the Detroit Lions, who won 19-15 to halt the Vikings' unbeaten start.

Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups.

Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was taken to hospital to be treated for a neck injury suffered while tackling tight end TJ Hockenson in the fourth quarter.

The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24.

Patrick Mahomes threw for three touchdowns and 321 yards but that was not enough for the Chiefs as the Broncos' defence made a goal-line stand at the death to clinch victory.

The Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) are in charge of the AFC South after romping to a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, who look set for a rebuild.

After firing their general manager and trading two key players in the past two weeks, the Colts are reportedly in talks over trading star running back Jonathan Taylor.

Meanwhile, the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) beat the Cleveland Browns 26-7 to go top of the AFC North.

Another of Pittsburgh's divisional rivals, the Cincinnati Bengals, made hard work of it before beating the Tennessee Titans 43-36 in overtime.

Despite being intercepted three times by Tennessee's Amani Hooker, Burrow became the first player in 75 years - and only the second ever after Norm van Brocklin's 554 passing yards in a 1951 game - to record more than 450 passing yards, five touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown in a single game.

After a mixed start to the season, the former first overall draft pick has also become the first quarterback in NFL history to register a 70% completion percentage plus touchdown passes in three consecutive games.

Burrow and his high-powered offence are in ominous form as they seek a Super Bowl return and host Pittsburgh in two weeks.

While Cincinnati's offence relies on its passing game and receivers, many of the NFL's running backs grabbed the spotlight on Sunday.

For the first time since 2003, at least six players had 140 rushing yards on the same day, including Bucky Irving (170) and Kenneth Gainwell (140) as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0.

Torrential rain in Florida made handling conditions difficult so Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes, completing none of them.

Instead he spent most of the day handing the ball to Irving or Gainwell as the Bucs racked up a team-record 324 rushing yards.

They also became the first team to have zero pass completions since 1974 – and just the second in the Super Bowl era.

Tyler Allgeier was the running back who starred for the Arizona Cardinals, rushing for 147 yards at the Dallas Cowboys.

But it was eccentric back-up quarterback Gardner Minshew who helped turn the game in Arizona's favour after replacing an ineffective Jacoby Brissett with the Cardinals trailing 17-3 late in the third quarter.

After being a late draft pick by Jacksonville in 2019, Minshew has spent most of his career as a back-up and in the off-season Arizona became his sixth team in eight years.

He made a thrilling debut, though, becoming the first quarterback this season to throw three touchdown passes in a fourth quarter.

That tied the game at the death, and although recent hero Chad Ryland failed to kick the extra point, he redeemed himself in overtime with a field goal to win 33-30.

It is only the second time Dallas have ever lost when leading by 10 points inside the final three minutes and leaves them 3-5.

It also heaps pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, with outspoken team owner Jerry Jones saying: "It's an indictment of the whole show".

articles.title: In 1974, the Buffalo Bills won an NFL game without completing a pass; 52 years later, Baker Mayfield's Buccaneers repeated the feat in a 16-0 victory
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off an unusual NFL feat on Sunday, November 1. They beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 without completing a single pass.
articles.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off an unusual NFL feat on Sunday, November 1. They beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 without completing a single pass. Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3, but his team found enough offense on the ground to secure its second straight win. It was the first time in 52 years that an NFL team had won without recording a completion. The last team to do it was the Buffalo Bills in 1974.Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell led Tampa Bay's attack at Raymond James Stadium. Their career-high rushing performances helped the Buccaneers control a rain-soaked divisional matchup. Meanwhile, the defense made sure Atlanta never found its way onto the scoreboard.Baker Mayfield's Buccaneers use 324 rushing yards to shut out FalconsHeavy rain and strong winds made passing difficult throughout Sunday's game. Tampa Bay quickly recognised the conditions and adjusted its offensive approach. Instead of asking Mayfield to force throws through the weather, the Buccaneers kept attacking on the ground.Mayfield attempted just two passes in the first half and one after the break. His first attempt came with 7:53 remaining in the opening quarter. It nearly turned into a 28-yard touchdown, but receiver Ted Hurst dropped the ball. Mayfield attempted another pass later in the quarter before making his final attempt early in the third period.There was little reason to keep throwing. Tampa Bay was finding plenty of room against Atlanta's defense, and its running backs continued to produce big plays.Bucky Irving finished with a career-high 170 rushing yards on 27 carries. Kenneth Gainwell also recorded a career best, adding 140 yards on 25 attempts. Together, the two running backs produced 310 yards, while Mayfield contributed another 14 rushing yards.Their biggest contribution came on Tampa Bay's lone touchdown drive. Irving broke away for a 46-yard run, while Gainwell added a 28-yard gain. The two combined for 90 yards on six carries during the drive before Irving finished it with a four-yard touchdown run in the third quarter.Chase McLaughlin handled the other scoring opportunities. The kicker converted three field goals from 46, 34 and 42 yards to help Tampa Bay build its 16-point lead.The Buccaneers finished with 324 rushing yards, setting a new franchise single-game record. They also recorded negative net passing yards, making the performance even more unusual. It was a remarkable turnaround for an offense that had managed only 64 passing yards in its previous victory.Mayfield focused on managing the offense rather than worrying about his passing numbers. Tampa Bay also used shotgun and pistol formations to make handling the ball easier in the wet conditions."It's winning -- that's the way I think about it. We won," Mayfield said after Sunday's game, according to the Buccaneers' postgame interview. He also made his approach clear, adding, "I will do whatever it takes to win. That's all that matters to me."Buffalo Bills last achieved the rare NFL feat in 1974 as Falcons struggleWhile Tampa Bay's running game did most of the offensive work, its defense made sure the Falcons could not recover. Michael Penix Jr. struggled throughout the afternoon and threw four interceptions. He finished with eight completions for 125 yards, with three of his interceptions coming in the first half.Atlanta's passing problems made the game even harder to manage. Penix did not record more completions than interceptions until midway through the third quarter. The Falcons could not establish a passing rhythm, while Tampa Bay continued to control the game through its ground attack.The two teams combined for only eight completions. That was the fewest in an NFL game since December 17, 1978, when the Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Colts also combined for eight.The historical comparison goes back to September 29, 1974. On that day, the Buffalo Bills defeated the Baltimore Colts 16-12 without completing a pass. Quarterback Joe Ferguson attempted only two passes, and both fell incomplete. Buffalo relied on its rushing attack, with Ferguson and Jim Braxton scoring touchdowns on the ground.More than five decades later, Tampa Bay became the second team in the Super Bowl era to win without a completion. The Buccaneers also became the first team since the 1945 Pittsburgh Steelers to win by at least 10 points without completing a pass. Pittsburgh had shut out the Chicago Cardinals 23-0.Sunday's performance also continued an impressive run for Tampa Bay's rushing attack. The Buccaneers have recorded 925 rushing yards over their last four games, the most in a four-game stretch in franchise history. Irving and Gainwell have given the offense another way to move the ball, even when Mayfield cannot find his receivers.The 16-0 victory moved Tampa Bay to 3-5 and gave the team back-to-back divisional wins after its previous victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers are now level with Atlanta in the NFC South win column, keeping themselves in the division race despite their losing record.Speaking after Sunday's victory, head coach Todd Bowles acknowledged that his team still had plenty of work ahead. According to the Buccaneers' postgame transcript, he said, "I told them to keep their shovels close because we have a lot more digging to do, but it gets us back in it."Mayfield will likely have to return to a bigger passing role in the coming weeks. However, against Atlanta, Tampa Bay showed that its running game and defense could carry the offense when the weather made throwing nearly impossible.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Don’t look for loopholes”: Travis Kelce’s charitable efforts come under scrutiny as 87 & Running faces questions over $1.1 million in spending
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, might have been a force to be reckoned with on the field but his name has dominated
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, might have been a force to be reckoned with on the field but his name has dominated headlines related to a few controversial issues related to his charity, 87 & Running. While Travis Kelce’s charity has consistently worked towards the communities of Kansas City, it has landed the star player in some trouble.Travis Kelce’s foundation 87 and Running finds itself allegedly involved in controversial issuesEarlier this year, there had been reports that Travis Kelce’s charity 87 & Running’s tax filings revealed that the foundation spent roughly $1.1 million of the $1.5 million it raised.But only about 41% of that money actually went toward charitable programming, while the remainder went to overhead costs.In an interview with The Arizona Republic, CharityWatch CEO and Executive Director, Laurie Styron, weighed in on Travis Kelce’s charity’s controversy as she said, “It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity…”CharityWatch CEO and Executive Director, Laurie Styron, added, “That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong…”CharityWatch CEO and Executive Director, Laurie Styron, continued, “Players and their managers need to stop using charities this way. Don’t get creative. Don’t look for loopholes. If you establish a charity, stop mixing in business interests or using friends to operate it. Do it the right way or don’t do it at all. There are a lot of ways for players to give back without founding their own charity.”However, neither the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end Travis Kelce nor his foundation, 87 & Running, has made any public statements about the issues.Though Travis Kelce’s foundation, 87 & Running’s name has found itself attached to controversial issues, the star player has continued to work towards the communities in Kansas City.Despite his busy life on the field, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end has continued to take out time for the people of Kansas City who need his support.Travis Kelce remains focused even as the Kansas City Chiefs records brutal losses in the last two matchesWhile Travis Kelce has been a reliable player on the field for the Kansas City Chiefs, the team has recorded two consecutive losses in the last two matches.This has sparked concern about the team’s performance but Travis Kelce has largely stayed away from commenting on the mess.After a slow run on the field in the last season, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce recorded 29 receptions for 410 yards and two touchdowns across seven games through Week 8.For now, all eyes remain on the Super Bowl champion as he gears up for the Week 8 clash.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Aaron Rodgers has already thrown 1,871 yards for Pittsburgh; what his 2026 Steelers numbers reveal about their Super Bowl chances
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has 1,871 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions through eight games.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has 1,871 passing yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions through eight games. The Steelers are 6-2, have won four in a row and lead the AFC North going into their Week 9 bye. Those totals look healthy, but the story behind them is more mixed. Jaylen Warren and the defense drove the latest win over Cleveland, and Mason Rudolph played the final snaps. Here is what Rodgers’ numbers say about a title run.What Aaron Rodgers’ 1,871 yards say about the Steelers’ offenseAaron Rodgers has completed 175 of 288 passes, or 60.8 percent, for 6.5 yards per attempt. His passer rating is 86.2. Spread over 17 games, his yardage lands near 3,980. That is close to last season, when he finished eighth in the league in yards and tied for seventh in touchdown passes.Volume is not the issue. Efficiency is. His 6.5 yards per attempt sits below last year’s 6.8, a mark that ranked 23rd. Pro Football Focus had him 25th among 35 qualified quarterbacks in overall grade through Week 7. Sumer Sports, which tracks how much each play helps or hurts a drive, has his passing in negative territory over that stretch.So the box score is kinder than the film. He throws a lot and finds the end zone often enough, but the offense is not yet getting big gains from his arm on a steady basis. Pittsburgh has 1,699 passing yards as a team through seven games, only slightly more than the 1,610 its opponents have managed.Why his best and worst days look so differentThe swings are the real pattern. In Week 2, New England beat Pittsburgh 20-3, and Rodgers went 23 of 39 for 187 yards with an interception and no touchdowns.Then came a hot run. He threw for 292 yards and three scores against Cincinnati, 299 and three at Cleveland, then 235 and three against Indianapolis. ESPN noted that no quarterback aged 41 or older had ever thrown three touchdowns in three straight games within a season. Each of his scores against the Bengals traveled at least 20 air yards, which was a first for him as a Steeler.He also dragged the team back from 13 down in the fourth quarter against Tampa Bay, finishing 33 of 49 for 253 yards in an overtime win. Last Sunday he went 13 of 25 for 172 yards, the lowest totals of his season, and threw no touchdown.Protection explains a lot of the gap. Rodgers has been sacked 23 times, close to three a game, and the Week 4 loss in Cleveland included five of them. His time to throw averages about 2.6 seconds, so he is not holding the ball long. The pressure is arriving quickly, and when the line holds, he looks like a quarterback who can still win games.Is the run game now carrying Pittsburgh?Over the last month, yes. Warren ran for 143 yards and a touchdown against the Browns, tying his career high. The Steelers piled up 200 rushing yards as a team, and all three of their touchdowns came on the ground. Warren had 561 rushing yards before that game, and he has four 100-yard days since Week 3.The defense matched that. Pittsburgh sacked Deshaun Watson eight times, a season high, and T.J. Watt came into the game with 7.5 sacks this year. Cleveland ran for only 34 yards. Reports after the game said the Steelers have allowed just one second-half touchdown all season.This changes Rodgers’ job. He no longer has to rescue every drive, which suits a 42-year-old with an arm that works best in short bursts. Coach Mike McCarthy still said his team left points on the field, and that is fair. The pass game has to produce more explosive plays than it has. DK Metcalf leads receivers with 374 yards, and Warren and rookie Germie Bernard are the next two names, which shows how spread out and modest the target share has been.It also means the formula depends on staying ahead. Running the ball works when the score is close. Rodgers, with his history of late comebacks, is the safety net for the games where it is not.How real are the Steelers’ Super Bowl chances?The market started out doubtful. Before the season, books listed Pittsburgh anywhere from about +6000 to +10000, which put them well outside the top tier. A 6-2 record and first place in the division have helped, but the current favorites are still teams like the Rams and Bills, and Pittsburgh has not been priced like one of them since.What gives the case some weight is the shape of the team. A strong run game, a defense that pressures the passer and a veteran quarterback who has seen every look is a recognizable playoff profile. Rodgers has not won a title since the 2010 season with Green Bay. The Steelers last did it after the 2008 season. Super Bowl LXI is on February 14 at SoFi Stadium.The weak points are clear enough. The passing game needs more explosive plays, the offensive line needs to cut those sacks, and Rodgers needs more nights like Week 5 than Week 8. He is also working on a one-year, $22.5 million deal, so every game carries some urgency.The next test comes in Week 10 at Cincinnati on Sunday night. There is a milestone in play too. Rodgers needs roughly 1,855 more yards to reach 70,000 for his career. At his current pace, that would take about eight more games, which puts it inside this regular season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes' $999 fitness business and Patrick Mahomes' $504 million Chiefs contract fuel family fortune
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes has built a public profile that reaches well beyond her marriage to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has built a public profile that reaches well beyond her marriage to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. From professional soccer and fitness entrepreneurship to sports ownership and modelling, she has turned several opportunities into a growing business portfolio. While there is no verified public figure for her personal net worth, her career offers plenty of clues about how she earns her money. Her connection to one of the NFL's biggest stars has brought additional attention, but Brittany has also worked to establish an identity of her own.Brittany Mahomes' net worth and business ventures explainedPutting an exact price tag on Brittany Mahomes' wealth is difficult because she has not publicly disclosed her finances, and reliable estimates of her personal net worth are unavailable. Still, her business interests reveal several sources of income.In 2019, she launched Brittany Lynne Fitness, a workout brand built around her background in sports and fitness. Its TUF BRITT programme costs $999 and provides four workouts per week over a four-week period. The programme also requires participants to have access to a gym.Modelling has opened another door. Brittany appeared in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue in 2024 and returned for a digital cover in 2026. She has also secured commercial opportunities with brands such as Adidas and CommunityAmerica Credit Union, while working as an Amazon affiliate partner.Her biggest sports-related venture is the Kansas City Current. Brittany is a founding co-owner of the NWSL club and also serves on the league's advisory board. Patrick joined the ownership group in 2023, becoming the first active NFL player to hold equity in an NWSL franchise.With more than two million Instagram followers, Brittany also has a strong platform for brand partnerships and public appearances.Brittany Mahomes' soccer career, family life and Patrick's $504 million contractBefore becoming a familiar face in the NFL community, Brittany built her sporting career on the soccer field. She earned a kinesiology degree from the University of Texas at Tyler, where she scored 31 goals in 74 games. She also competed in two Division III Women's Soccer Championships and became the first player in the programme's history to record three hat tricks.She later played professionally in Iceland for Afturelding/Fram, although her overseas career lasted just one year. In January 2026, her achievements earned her a place in the Texas-Tyler Hall of Fame.Away from business, Brittany and Patrick share three children: Sterling, Patrick III and Golden. Their relationship began in high school, long before Patrick became an NFL superstar.“I fall in love with my wife all over again every time I see her parenting,” Patrick told TODAY in 2023. “My daughter is at that age where she wants both of us to put her to sleep. I’ll sit back and watch her read to (Sterling), and those are the moments I’ll always remember.”Patrick's earnings also form an important part of the family's financial picture. In June 2026, he signed a reworked eight-year, $504 million contract with the Chiefs. According to Spotrac, his career earnings had already exceeded $232 million entering the 2026 season.While Patrick's NFL fortune attracts much of the attention, Brittany's fitness business, modelling work and ownership stake give her a separate professional identity.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jack Campbell injury update: Detroit Lions linebacker lay motionless after taking a hard hit on his helmet from Minnesota Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions became the first team to defeat the league’s last remaining unbeaten team, the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body: The Detroit Lions became the first team to defeat the league’s last remaining unbeaten team, the Minnesota Vikings. But they lost their linebacker Jack Campbell to a brutal injury in the fourth quarter of the Lions’ 19-15 victory over the Vikings.“Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family,” Detroit head coach Dan Campbell said after the game. “He’s being taken care of. We’ll keep you updated as this thing goes. But we are thinking about him. We’re thinking about him.”The team later said in a statement, “Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them.”What happened to Jack Campbell?Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson caught the ball, but three Detroit Lions players jumped on him, trying to snatch it away. Eric O’Neill came from one side, Chuck Clark from the other, and Jack Campbell changed his route and came from the third side.All three Lions players surrounded the Vikings player in a big-time impactful sandwich play. The only fault? The one who looked like he had the least impact lay paralyzed on the ground. That was Jack Campbell.O’Neill went for Hockenson’s torso, Clark went for the ball, while Campbell went for Hockenson’s leg. Hockenson landed on O’Neill;Clark stayed away from the impact and didn’t fall to the ground, but the hard helmet hit Campbell took from Hockenson’s thigh knocked him straight to his stomach, motionless. His head struck Hockenson and his neck twisted backward awkwardly.O’Neill also took a hard hit to the helmet from Hockenson’s side torso, but because Hockenson was also trying to change route with Campbell, Campbell took the hardest hit to the helmet from Hockenson’s thigh.Campbell immediately let go of Hockenson’s legs and fell motionless on his stomach. Medical personnel arrived at his spot. They surrounded him for nine minutes before strapping him to a backboard.He was carefully lifted. He may have sustained a neck injury. He did not signal to the Ford Field crowd as they took him away from the gridiron toward the tunnel on a cart.Neck injury or prior concussionAccording to the Associated Press, the 26-year-old linebacker Jack Campbell stayed overnight at a local hospital for continued evaluation and monitoring of a neck injury.As pointed out by Heavy Sports, a board-certified doctor, Jimmy Liao, suggested that Campbell may have suffered a concussive injury three minutes prior to the hit that left him motionless.“Jack Campbell injury video: I’m including an earlier play from 3 minutes prior that was suspicious for a predecessor concussion. Hopefully, only a concussion here. Did not get hit in top of helmet so hopefully no spinal issue and just precaution,” Liao wrote on X.Aidan Hutchinson and Dan Campbell got emotionalThe former Iowa star has quite an impact on everyone around him. When Jack Campbell was being carted off, the camera focused on his teammates, particularly Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.Hutchinson was very emotional, but he tried his best to lead the team. At the postgame locker room speech, head coach Dan Campbell was almost in tears; he asked everyone on the team to take a knee to pray for Campbell.“I’m gonna lower this mood a little bit. I do not have any more information on Jack. We don’t know anything else at this point. But here’s what I wanna do, man. We’re gonna take a knee. Now, I wanna pray for Jack. Let's keep him in our thoughts and prayers,” the coach said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes breaks silence on controversial referee decision as  Chiefs’ second consecutive loss sparks fresh concerns
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, started the new season strong with an impressive run on the field.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, started the new season strong with an impressive run on the field. But the team has now recorded two consecutive losses against the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos. Amid the brutal loss in Week 7, Patrick Mahomes has reflected on the late game false start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore.Patrick Mahomes reacts to the controversial call which led the Kansas City Chiefs to lose against the Denver BroncosA few hours ago, as the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback Patrick Mahomes spoke to reporters after the loss against the Denver Broncos, he said, "I have not seen it, but like it didn't surprise me or catch me or anything like that, so it couldn't have been big, but it was called…”The three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player added, "I mean, at the end of the day, you have to go with whatever is called, but a lot of times in those big moments the little stuff doesn't get called like that."The Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid also reacted to the controversial call at the game against the Denver Broncos as he said, "I didn't see it,...I saw him move his head, but I didn't see [a false start]."What really happened at the game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos?For the unversed, with 4 seconds left in the game and the Kansas City Chiefs trailing the Denver Broncos 28-24, Patrick Mahomes threw what looked like a game winning touchdown pass to wide receiver Rashee Rice.However, the referees threw a flag and called a false start penalty on the Kansas City Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore. The penalty canceled the touchdown and pushed the Chiefs back 5 yards.On the very next play, Patrick Mahomes was sacked, ending the game as it marked the Kansas City Chiefs’ second consecutive loss in the new season after losing to the Seattle Seahawks last weekend.Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes also reacted to it as she took to her social media to make a post that read as, “You can’t tell me you call that on a game-winning TD, oh wait yeah I can ’cause it’s us.”Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes added, “The weakest call I have ever seen. You can’t tell me otherwise.”Through the first seven games of the 2026 NFL season, Patrick Mahomes has recorded 1,795 yards, 12 touchdowns, and only 4 interceptions.It seems the star quarterback has recovered pretty well after his brutal injuries in the last season as he remains focused on the field for the Week 7 clash against the New York Jets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Complete BS,' Jayden Daniels Calls Out Commanders After Win vs. Eagles amid Viral Video of Sideline
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was almost disgusted to see his team climb into a 10-0 hole against the shorthanded Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was almost disgusted to see his team climb into a 10-0 hole against the shorthanded Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night.

"Honestly, it was just complete BS, the way we started," he said after the 27-10 win, per The Athletic's David Aldridge .

At one point in the first half, Daniels had a spirited chat with his offensive linemen on the sideline.

"The coaches could beat a dead horse all they want," he said. "At the end of the day, you have to take accountability. You have to focus. You can't have mental lapses. Ultimately, it's on us."

The Commanders had a week off to reset following a 1-4-1 start, and Philly presented a great opportunity to get things right on the field. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is likely sidelined for the year, and a number of other key players are banged up .

That magnified the frustration from Washington's start. The team missed a field goal on its first drive, had a three-and-out, and then saw the next possession begin with back-to-back penalties before a fumble by tight end Chig Okonkwo on the first play.

From the second quarter on, it was a much different story. The Commanders ratcheted up the defense and had more success moving the ball. They ultimately out-gained Philadelphia 339-268 and were plus-one in turnover margin.

"You've heard me talk a lot about four quarters," coach Dan Quinn said. "I thought tonight, we nailed three. We need all four. That's how it needs to go down."

The result was a step in the right direction for a team that desperately needed a win. There are still some issues for Quinn and his staff to iron out when tricky matchups against the Los Angeles Rams, New York Giants and Cincinnati Bengals are ahead.

articles.title: Tom Brady reportedly wants FOX Sports to cut his on air expletive from NFL pregame coverage
articles.summary: This is Tom Brady’s third year as an NFL broadcaster, but he still seems to have no control over his cursing!
articles.body: This is Tom Brady’s third year as an NFL broadcaster, but he still seems to have no control over his cursing! The seven-time Super Bowl champion found himself in yet another awkward live-television moment when he dropped an expletive during FOX’s NFL pregame coverage.To top it off, he even directed the cameraman, whoever was recording him, or the channel perhaps, to cut that part off where he cursed.The New England Patriots legend once again blurted out an “oh, sh*t!” on air, thereby marking the second instance this season that the former quarterback forgot about his live microphone.Tom Brady swears on air for the second time, this time with Drew Brees and not Jayden DanielsIt’s one thing to speak your mind, and it’s another to say something expletive live on air. So many millions of people were listening to Tom Brady. So many people are trying to walk his path.And if he sets this as an everyday example - yes, who doesn’t utter that “oh, sh*t” at least seven times a day - but if the NFL broadcaster sets that as an everyday example live on air? It could become a norm…it could soon be on everybody’s tongue. Like, it’s extremely normal and natural to utter that expletive.Anyhow, unlike Brady’s previous incident involving the Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels - where he could not ask the cameraman or whoever was recording him to cut it, because he was playcalling - we could just hear him use that expletive, where he did say, “excuse me” immediately after uttering the expletive.But still that doesn’t change the premise of uttering an expletive live on air. As if it’s some podcast show where real emotions are expressed. Who’s to blame?Anyhow, this time, the reaction came during a lighthearted quiz with fellow NFL legend Drew Brees. The other broadcasters laughed it off, saying, “he’s learning.” How long will it take for the seven-time Super Bowl champion to learn how to not use an expletive on air? Just speculating here.Tom Brady drops another expletive word during FOX NFL Sunday segmentThe incident took place on November 1 during FOX Sports’ NFL pregame show. Legendary quarterbacks Tom Brady and Drew Brees participated in a quiz segment called “Who’s in Third?”The quiz tested their knowledge of various all-time NFL quarterback records. During one question, the seven-time Super Bowl champion was asked to identify the quarterback with the third-most career games with at least 300 passing yards.Drew Brees took up the first spot with 123 career games with over 300 passing yards, while Brady took up the second spot with 113 such performances. When they asked for the third spot, Brady inadvertently responded, “Brees!” Then someone told him, “Brees is No. 1, he can’t be 1 and 3.”Brady realized his mistake and immediately uttered, “Oh, sh*t!” Brady’s reaction quickly prompted Michael Strahan and Terry Bradshaw to burst out laughing - loudly.Brady then correctly guessed, “Peyton Manning,” as the third quarterback to have the most career games recording at least 300 passing yards - 93. But even if Brady guessed it right the second time, his “oh, sh*t” reaction was not reportedly forgotten by the fellow broadcasters.They reminded him of it at the end of the quiz round. “We let you get away with one, by the way, Tom,” said one. “Hey, that’s what live TV is about. You know it’s live,” said another. “He’s learning. He’s learning,” commented a third.Jayden Daniels injury replay leaves Tom Brady stunnedThe very first trigger of the expletive word “oh, sh*t” came during September 20’s week 2 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders.While calling the game, Tom Brady reacted to a replay of Jayden Daniels’ elbow injury. Daniels’ arm bent awkwardly as he fell to the ground to brace himself after an offensive lineman stepped on him.Looking at the shocking replay, Brady blurted out the expletive word, “oh, sh*t.” But he immediately apologized to his listeners, “Excuse me. I was not expecting to see that.”Tom Brady could face FCC consequencesFirst in September 2026, then in November 2026. Tom Brady’s repeated slip-ups raise questions about broadcast regulations.According to Front Office Sports, the Federal Communications Commission prohibits indecent and profane language on broadcast television between 6 AM and 10 PM, especially when children could be watching.If broadcasters violate its rules, the FCC could investigate complaints and issue warnings, admonishments, or fines. However, there has been no confirmation of disciplinary action against the NFL legend following either of the two incidents in which he uttered the expletive in haste. As if speaking your mind.The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is currently in his third season as FOX Sports’ lead NFL analyst. He signed a 10-year, $375 million broadcasting agreement with the network. His current verbal slip is yet another viral moment from his short-spanned broadcasting career. “He’s learning,” remember?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lions LB Jack Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury after being carted off, immobilized on backboard
articles.summary: Campbell, who went down after a tackle, was tended to for several minutes by trainers before being immobilized and loaded onto the cart.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions' victory over the Minnesota Vikings took a scary turn after linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off after going down on a tackle in the second half.

The Lions later announced that Campbell was taken to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. He is resting and will remain hospitalized overnight.

Both Campbell and linebacker Jimmy Rolder went down on the same play in the fourth quarter, with both defenders staying on the ground while lying facedown. Rolder was able to get up, while Campbell stayed down for a long time, facedown with his arms at his sides.

Campbell was surrounded by staff and tended to for several minutes before being loaded onto a backboard while immobilized. He was then carted off into the locker room.

The entire Lions team gathered around Campbell while he was being loaded onto the stretcher, with several players visibly emotional. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, who is a defensive captain alongside Campbell, appeared to be crying.

Campbell's neck injury occurred on a seemingly routine tackle on T.J. Hockenson shortly after the start of the fourth quarter. It was not immediately clear what had happened, but it was quickly clear that it was serious.

Detroit went on to win 19-15 , handing the Vikings their first loss of the season. Postgame , Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the linebacker is "being taken care of" but had no additional information about his condition.

Campbell is in his fourth season in the league this fall. The former Iowa standout, who the Lions selected with the No. 18 overall pick in 2023, had three total tackles in their win on Sunday. He's up to 57 on the season.

articles.title: Watch Viral Videos of Caleb Downs Getting Pancaked by Froholdt, Trolled by McBride in Cowboys' Loss
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs had an outing he'd wish to forget in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs had an outing he'd wish to forget in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

In addition to being placed in concussion protocol, Downs was on the wrong end of a pair of viral videos.

Early in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game, Downs was pancaked and taken for a ride by Cardinals center Hjalte Froholdt on a 52-yard run by Tyler Allgeier:

Daniels, Commanders Win Despite 'BS' Start

If that wasn't bad enough, Cardinals star tight end Trey McBride was heard trolling Downs after catching a pass over him, yelling, "You a first-rounder? For what?"

In fairness to Downs, he's been off to a strong start in his first year in the NFL, leading the Cowboys with 52 total tackles while adding three forced fumbles and a sack.

Downs and the Cowboys (3-5) will try to bounce back when they face the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) in Week 9.

articles.title: Cousins, Flacco, Daniel Jones Trades Pitched by NFL Insider After Lamar Jackson's Injury for Ravens
articles.summary: Two notable NFL insiders don't believe the Baltimore Ravens can sit idly by with franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson set to miss multiple weeks.
articles.body:
Two notable NFL insiders don't believe the Baltimore Ravens can sit idly by with franchise quarterback Lamar Jackson set to miss multiple weeks.

Following Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills, coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson is headed for injured reserve due to a thumb injury. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was also hurt in the defeat, forcing the team to turn to third-stringer Joe Fagnano.

The Athletic's Mike Sando asserted the Ravens "need to find a quarterback, unless they're willing to pack it in."

He cast doubt on one potential option, questioning whether the Las Vegas Raiders would entertain a Kirk Cousins trade after the offseason saga surrounding Maxx Crosby.

Sando also argued Cousins' solid production (2,124 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions) may not be indicative of how he'd fare elsewhere. He had already played under Raiders coach Klint Kubiak before he signed with Las Vegas.

Sando's colleague Michael Silver threw out the idea of a reunion with Joe Flacco or acquiring the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones or Chicago Bears' Tyson Bagent.

The Colts continue to sink further after having already traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Maybe they'd be willing to unload Jones' contract and start over at quarterback.

Chicago can afford to deal Bagent when it also has Case Keenum on the roster. Keenum is arguably a better backup anyway. Bagent was coached by Baltimore offensive coordinator Declan Doyle last year, which is a factor to consider.

Like Cousins, Flacco could be a nonstarter. The Cincinnati Bengals will need a lot of convincing to send him to a division rival with playoff aspirations.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Huntley "suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury." Assuming he, like Jackson, will miss multiple games, Baltimore can't afford to move forward with Fagnano. The undrafted free agent went 10-of-21 for 91 yards and an interception against Buffalo.

The fact that Bagent and Flacco are being floated as solutions illustrates the Ravens' bind, though.

There aren't a lot of great QB options on the trade market right now and certainly not one who inspires a ton of confidence to lead a playoff push in the second half.

articles.title: Joe Burrow joins an exclusive NFL club after throwing six touchdowns, but one historic stat comes with a warning
articles.summary: Joe Burrow delivered one of the most remarkable performances of his NFL career on Sunday, leading the Cincinnati Bengals to a 43-36 overtime win over the
articles.body: Joe Burrow delivered one of the most remarkable performances of his NFL career on Sunday, leading the Cincinnati Bengals to a 43-36 overtime win over the Tennessee Titans despite throwing three interceptions. Burrow finished with 462 passing yards, five touchdown passes and a rushing score, becoming only the second quarterback since 1951 to record a rare combination of passing and rushing numbers. The victory pushed Cincinnati to 5-2, but the turnovers exposed a problem that could prove costly against stronger opponents. Burrow’s brilliance rescued the Bengals. His mistakes nearly handed Tennessee the game.Joe Burrow matches a historic NFL feat in Bengals’ overtime winJoe Burrow’s performance placed him alongside Hall of Fame quarterback Norm Van Brocklin in a statistical category that has stood untouched for 75 years. According to ESPN Insights, Burrow became the first quarterback since 1951 to record at least 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown in a game.Van Brocklin achieved the feat while playing for the Los Angeles Rams in 1951, when he threw for a then-record 554 yards against the New York Yanks. Burrow joined that exclusive company with a performance that combined outstanding production with an unusual number of costly errors.The Bengals needed nearly every bit of his output. Tennessee opened a 13-0 lead and continued to challenge Cincinnati throughout a game that featured repeated changes in momentum. Burrow found Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for key scores, then connected with Higgins for an 18-yard touchdown with 1:17 remaining to tie the game at 36.In overtime, Burrow took control again. He led Cincinnati on a 70-yard drive before running nine yards into the end zone for the winning score. The Bengals improved to 5-2, their best start at this stage of a season since 2021.His supporting cast also delivered. Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns, while Chase added 11 receptions for 141 yards and a score. Their production helped Cincinnati survive a game in which its quarterback repeatedly gave Tennessee opportunities to take control.Three interceptions raise concerns despite Joe Burrow’s six touchdownsThe record-setting numbers came with a clear warning. Titans safety Amani Hooker intercepted Burrow three times, turning a potentially dominant quarterback display into a much tighter contest than Cincinnati would have wanted.Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes, but the interceptions exposed the danger of relying on his ability to repair mistakes. Cincinnati also lost a fumble, giving the team four turnovers overall. Against a more efficient opponent, that kind of performance could easily end in defeat.Burrow did not dismiss the problem after the game. “I felt like we moved it pretty well all game. We had four turnovers. It’s hard to win that way. Today we did, but you can’t make a living like that,” he said.That assessment matters more than the historic milestone. Cincinnati has now rallied from a 13-point first-half deficit in consecutive games, showing resilience but also leaving itself with little margin for error. The Bengals face the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid next week, and Burrow will need to keep producing while protecting the football.Sunday proved that Burrow can carry Cincinnati through a difficult afternoon. It also showed why the Bengals cannot expect six-touchdown performances to cover every mistake.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin calls out Cowboys’ mentality after costly collapse against Cardinals
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin criticizes Dallas Cowboys for losing despite leading late in the game.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of their most painful defeats of the 2026 NFL season after blowing a 10-point lead against the Arizona Cardinals . Their 33-30 overtime loss on Sunday also drew sharp criticism from Mike Tomlin.

Speaking on ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown, the former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach questioned Dallas' mentality during the closing stages. Tomlin said the Cowboys lacked players willing to take responsibility when the game was on the line.

"I saw a bunch of blinkers," Tomlin said. "And what I mean by that, I say if you're a blinker, cut your eyelids off. What I mean is you gotta relish the thick moments. You gotta want to make the play as an individual and as a unit within a team."

Tomlin explained that Dallas needed individuals and units willing to make decisive plays. Instead, he saw a team that failed to respond when Arizona mounted its comeback.

"Watching the end of that game, I didn't see individuals or particular units that wanted to grab the bull by the horns and win the game," Tomlin said.

The Cowboys' defense struggled during the final minutes. However, Tomlin also questioned the offense's inability to take advantage of opportunities.

Mike Tomlin questions Cowboys' ability to finish games

Dallas had a short field after Arizona's unsuccessful onside kick late in regulation. However, the Cowboys failed to capitalize and went three-and-out in overtime.

"I see a team that doesn't have anybody that wants to be the unit to secure victory," Tomlin added. "They're blinkers. They gotta cut their eyelids off."

Tomlin thinks head coach Brian Schottenheimer must identify players willing to handle those pressure situations. He suggested changing responsibilities to give more opportunities to players who show that mentality.

"You gotta figure out who wants it, and you gotta shift your divisional labor to those that want it," Tomlin said. "And so knowledge of your team is a major component. But also, you got to challenge those guys individually and collectively. Tell them you're looking for that guy who wants to be it."

The collapse was particularly damaging because Dallas led by 14 points early in the fourth quarter. Arizona quarterback Gardner Minshew led a late touchdown drive, while kicker Chad Ryland eventually secured the victory with a 42-yard field goal.

The Cowboys finished with only 261 total yards, compared to Arizona's 467. Dak Prescott called the defeat one of the toughest losses he had experienced, saying, "No other words for it really, other than really, really disappointing, frustrating."

Dallas dropped to 3-5, leaving little room for further mistakes.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty is on the bust-train to trades-ville
articles.summary: Ashton Jeanty might be an old school NFL Draft bust.
articles.body:
Ashton Jeanty was universally praised as a pick when the Las Vegas Raiders selected him with the 6th overall pick in 2025. It was a move made with foresight, understanding that it wasn't the team's year to land a quarterback — instead deciding to fix their running game first, knowing the passer would come.

Midway into Jeanty's second season, he's become an afterthought of the offense. This was most pronounced on Sunday against the Jets when Jeanty recorded just two carries for nine yards, in a game when the Raiders ran the ball 28 times. The precipitous fall in Jeanty's usage is being waved off by the coaching staff, but the devil is in the details: After running the ball 23 times in the season opener, Jeanty has gotten fewer and fewer carries each game. By October 11 he was down to 10 carries, then eight against the Rams, then Sunday.

Taking his spot in the offense has been Mike Washington Jr, who the Raiders took with a 4th round pick in 2026. It's becoming clear that Washington is head coach Klint Kubiak's favored running back of the two, increasing his usage rate before giving him the lion's share of the carries against the Jets. Washington has a more defined role inside the Raiders offense as a bigger, bruising, short-yardage back who Kubiak is using to punctuate his passing offense. Meanwhile Jeanty is a three-down back now stuck in an offense that doesn't really want or need him. Kubiak clearly selected "his guy" in the draft, and now Jeanty is already feeling like a vestige of a bygone era.

Of course, a helping of the blame belongs to Jeanty himself. Since arriving in the NFL he has struggled to make any appreciable impact, averaging a paltry 3.5 yards per carry, only scoring six career touchdowns, and only boasting a successful run on 42% of his carries. It's been easy to blame the woeful Raiders' offensive line, but there's also a reality here that Jeanty just isn't able to create for himself from the backfield, make people miss, or bowl people over — averaging just 1.9 yards after contact since arriving in the NFL, and even worse is his yard before contact which sits at 1.5 yards. That is the truly staggering number, because it shows that Jeanty isn't nearly as explosive as he was in college.

The Raiders sit at an impasse. Kubiak is an offensive coach who has never really shown a penchant for running the football. He deviated from his plan for one season in Seattle when the team won the Super Bowl, but outside of that his teams have ranked in the bottom third of the NFL in carries across his other three seasons as an offensive coordinator. It's clear that Las Vegas doesn't really have a use case for Jeanty at this point, and perhaps the best move at this point would be to accept that keeping him is trying to fit a square peg into a round hole, and move on.

As it stands we have several contenders in dire need of a running back, all of whom might believe they could be the ones to revitalize Jeanty's career or had him highly graded in 2025, but fell short. A team like the Vikings makes a ton of sense, as would New England, or even Jacksonville — all of whom need help at running back and are positioned to make a playoff run. The question is whether or not the Raiders feel ready to pull off that Band-Aid yet, or more aptly — are they prepared for the fallout from making such a move?

Two things are clear: Jeanty is not playing good football, and the Raiders appear to have moved on.

articles.title: Bills to face a Vikings defense unlike any they have seen this season
articles.summary: In a battle of two 6-1 teams, ESPN is a big winner as it gets Bills vs. Vikings on Monday night. Here's a look ahead to the NFL game of the week.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK - The folks who run ESPN could not be more thrilled with how the Week 9 schedule has panned out for them because the bickering broadcast tandem of Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will be calling what is far and away the NFL's game of the week.

Entering the year everyone knew the Buffalo Bills were a Super Bowl contender and having started the season 6-1 that is proving to be correct, even though they are far from a flawless team as we saw in their 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens.

Conversely, not a whole lot was expected from the Minnesota Vikings who play in what might be the NFL's best division, the rugged NFC North, where the last-place Packers are 5-3. However, the Vikings won their first six games and were the last unbeaten team in the league before succumbing 19-15 on Sunday to the Lions .

Thus, ESPN gets a pair of division-leading 6-1 teams in a fascinating game in that when the Bills have the ball on offense it's going to be a matchup of great on great, and when the Vikings have the ball it will be the polar opposite, bad on bad.

Buffalo leads the NFL in scoring at 33.3 points per game thanks to a league-best 27 touchdowns and is second in yards per game (393.1) and yards per play (6.3). Not to diminish those numbers, but the Bills have done this against a fistful of mediocre to poor defenses. The best defense they faced based on points allowed per game is the Patriots who sit eighth with an average yield of 20.3. That was the only game they lost, one of only two where they failed to score at least 30 points.

Now Josh Allen and company will be facing the blitz-happy Vikings who lead the NFL by a whopping margin in fewest points allowed per game (13.3), sack percentage (10.96%) and QB pressure rate (45.8%) and second in yards (271.6), . The old bromide is that great defense beats great offense. We'll see, but the fact that the game is at U.S. Bank Stadium certainly gives the Vikings an advantage.

When those two great units are on the sidelines, we'll be watching the struggling Buffalo defense battling the equally struggling Minnesota offense. The Bills showed signs of life, albeit against Baltimore's third-string emergency QB Joe Fagnano, holding the Ravens to 10 points and 144 yards, and that performance helped them jump up in the rankings to 24th in points (25.9) and yards (352.1).

One would assume Kyler Murray will present more of a test, but the Vikings' offense ranks 27th in points (20.0), 29th in yards (279.4) and has scored just 11 touchdowns, ahead of only the dreadful Chargers who have nine.

15 best photos from Bills win over battered Ravens

Coach Joe Brady is going to need to put together an outstanding pass protection plan because Minnesota's pass rush is lethal and has been eviscerating opposing QBs all season. The Vikings blitz at a stunning rate of 71% per NextGenStats - the next-most blitzing team are the Bears who do it 40.6% of the time. And Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores sends those blitzes from every possible angle and you never know who's coming as 11 different players have at least half a sack, led by LBs Andrew Van Ginkel (6.5) and Dallas Turner (6).

They have one of the best WRs in the NFL in Justin Jefferson, but he has been neutered by this terrible offense and has just 28 catches on 40 targets for 335 yards. Murray has to take advantage of a Buffalo secondary that is still highly vulnerable when it isn't playing against a rookie emergency third-stringer making his NFL debut. This may be a game where the Bills' top CB, Christian Benford, travels with Jefferson and if so, that will be an intriguing subplot to watch.

Allen is a magician with his escape ability, but escaping Minnesota's pass rush is a whole different thing and not even Allen will be immune to the nonstop pressure, especially if RT Spencer Brown has to miss another game. The best way to back the Vikings off would be to feed James Cook and get him going against a run defense that ranks 17th at 116.7 yards per game and is tied for the sixth-most 10-plus yards runs allowed (24). Cook's 47.8% rushing success based on EPA is fourth-best in the NFL per Sumer Sports, his 5.12 average per carry is also fourth, and his 318 yards before first contact is No. 1.

The Vikings have faced three upper tier QBs and they were victorious in the first two weeks against the Packers' Jordan Love and the Bears' Caleb Williams, and then lost Sunday to the Lions' Jared Goff. In those three games their average net passing yield was just 148 yards thanks in part to 12 sacks for 85 yards, but the Lions provided the blueprint against Minnesota.

They pounded the Vikings on the ground for 230 yards, including 153 from Jahmyr Gibbs, and that's something the Bills can lean into with Cook who is every bit as dynamic as Gibbs and, in fact, has a higher average per carry.

As long as the Bills don't turn the ball over and/or kill themselves with penalties, they should become just the second team to reach 20 points against the Vikings, and that might be enough. And if there's one offense Buffalo's defense can match up with, it's Minnesota's which scored just nine points against an excellent Bears defense, but also managed only 15, 16 and 15 respectively against the lousy defenses of the Dolphins, Colts and Lions.

What time does the Bills vs Vikings game start?

Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. at U.S. Bank Stadium.

The Bills have opened as a 3-point favorite. The money line is Bills minus-150 (bet $150 to win $100) and Vikings plus-125 (bet $100 to win $125). The over-under is 46.5.

Cable/Network TV: ESPN. The game will be available on Spectrum channel 24 in Rochester, Syracuse, Albany, Binghamton, Utica and Elmira, and channel 30 in Buffalo.

How can you stream Bills vs Vikings game?

Online streaming services: With your TV subscription you can watch on your phone or tablet on ESPN.com, the ESPN mobile app, and ESPN Deportes. You can also watch games on NFL.com and the NFL mobile app, and you can subscribe to NFL+, the league's own streaming service, though you can't cast the games to your TV - you must watch on your phone or tablet.

TV streaming: You can also stream if you have subscriptions to Spectrum, DirecTV Choice, Fubo Sports , Sling, Vidgo, Hulu + Live TV, YouTubeTV + NFL Sunday Ticket.

On the radio: How to listen to the Bills vs Vikings game

You can listen on SiriusXM satellite radio on channel 193 (Bills feed) and channel 192 (Vikings feed), and on traditional radio, the Bills Radio Network has stations all across the state. Chris Brown has the play-by-play, Eric Wood is the analyst, and Steve Tasker is the sideline reporter. The network includes:

Sal Maiorana has covered the Buffalo Bills for four decades including 37 years as the full-time beat writer for the D&C, he has written numerous books about the history of the team, and he is also co-host of the BLEAV in Bills podcast/YouTube show. He can be reached at maiorana@gannett.com, and you can follow him on X @salmaiorana and on Bluesky @salmaiorana.bsky.social.
